properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to COPPERHEAD ENTERPRISES LLC in Hamilton Township, McKean County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/09/2026 to COPPERHEAD ENTERPRISES LLC in Hamilton Township, McKean county. CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: COPPERHEAD ENTERPRISES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/09/2026
Violation Code: CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
Violation ID: 8280937
Permit API: 083-47442
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/09/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to being notified by Chuck Rippey of Copperhead Enterprises on 7/8/26 of a crude oil spill due to a compromised subsurface gathering line located at the entrance of the spur road that accesses this conventional well. At the time of notification, according to Chuck, all wells on the lease had been shut in and containment measures were being placed throughout the impacted area.At the onset of this inspection, I met with Chuck who explained that the gathering line failed due to valves on the gathering lines at the tank battery unknowingly being closed by a suspected, unknown, third party prior to the lease being pumped on the afternoon of 7/8/26. It is estimated that the wells on the lease were pumping for 2-3 hours before the well tender drove towards this well and noticed the release at approximately 15:00. After ceasing production and shutting in the wells, Chuck reported the release to this WQSS via telephone.At the origin of the release, crude oil had sprayed onto the road bank and lower limbs of nearby trees. The majority of the crude oil migrated west/ northwest in a roadside ditch alongside Chappel Fork Road for approximately 400' before reaching a spring run that evolves into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Chappel Fork. Pockets of crude oil were observed in the spring run/UNT between where it intersects Chappel Fork Road and its confluence with Chappel Fork. Crude oil was also present in an approximate 750' stretch of Chappel Fork downslope of the stream's confluence with the aforementioned spring run/UNT.At this time, underflow dams, absorbent booms and pads have been placed throughout the impacted portions of the roadside ditch, spring run/UNT and Chappel Fork to contain the released product. Crews were in the process of recovering crude that was collecting behind the various containment measures and replacing saturated absorbents as needed. I advised Chuck to continue the ongoing practices and to place additional booms in slow moving water to minimize the potential for further migration downstream. After further progress is made with recovering the free crude, Chuck intends to excavate the contaminated soil at the origin of the release and replace the ruptured portion of the gathering line.At this time, the quantity of crude oil that was released is unknown. Chuck intends to stage the excavated contaminated soil on a lined pod at this well site until proper disposal at a landfill is arranged. Documentation of this disposal and confirmatory sampling of the impacted area after its remediation is expected to be provided to the Department in order for this incident to be considered closed.Upcoming inspections will be done throughout the remediation of this release to ensure suitable progress is being made.

Comments: During a routine complete inspection on 5/16/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3788146), I noted API 065-26269 did not have a well tag, equipment not necessary for production was being stored on site, and there was evidence of a production fluid release greater than 42 gallons.During a follow up inspection on 6/26/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3790440), I noted the well had a new well tag, the pipe was moved across the access road, and the spill area was seeded and mulched. The Department did not receive a response from the Notice of Violation with the operators intentions to use either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The Department did not receive tipping receipts or waste manifests associated with removal and disposal of contaminated soil from the spill. The tag violation was closed. The other violations remained open.As of today the Department still hasn't received tipping receipts and waste manifests regarding the clean up of this site. As I was leaving the Wheeler sites, I ran into Ray Hepler. He stated that the contaminated soil from the clean-up was added to the same truck containing soil from the southwest, and that he would eventually be providing tipping an manifest information. Mr. Hepler also stated he was unfamiliar with an Act 2 clean up. I told him I would email information about Act 2 when I returned to the office. The outstanding violations for this well will remain open.

Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/01/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 302(B)1 - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person failed to use methods or facilities necessary to control leachate, runoff, discharges and emissions from residual waste in accordance with DEP regulations.
Violation ID: 8269861
Permit API: 039-24118
Unconventional: No
County: Crawford
Municipality: East Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/01/2026
Comments: On 3/31/2026, Next Level Energy notified the Department that the Palermo 1 OG well (039-24118) sprayed an indeterminant amount of liquid mist out onto approximately of an acre while actively plugging the well. The Department dispatched Emergency Response to the site to evaluate.An onsite inspection in response to the complaint was conducted on 4/01/2026 by Elyse Henshaw, Water Quality Specialist, and Kyle Thomas, Oil and Gas Inspector. Upon arrival, Henshaw and Thomas found the impacted soil scraped up and piled around the well head. The soil was covered with tarps to prevent rainwater from carrying it from the site. Henshaw and Thomas conferred with representatives from Next Level Energy and Diversified to learn that the soil would be removed by the end of the week and plugging operations would resume. Henshaw and Thomas walked into the wooded area adjacent to the well site to find a waxy film on the leaf litter. Thomas believed the film was from the gel, a biodegradable material, used to put down hole to kill the well rather than residual crude oil. Henshaw and a representative from Diversified walked into the wooded area to determine the extent of the spray and did not find a sheen on top of the puddles within the area. Additionally, they utilized conductivity probes to determine no brine water was sprayed into the woods. They also tested multiple points in the area that had been scraped up to determine all contaminated soils had been removed. A small amount of brine water remained around the well head and will be removed when plugging operations conclude. Fresh topsoil, seed and mulch will be brought in to stabilize and restore the impacted area. On 04/07/2026 a copy of this report was sent to Diversified Production LLC at painspections@dgoc.com for their review.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 974738
Permit API: 081-20637
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cummings Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/07/2022
Comments: On November 7, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline completed an inspection to follow up with a reported spill of production fluid outside of containment at the EQT ARO LLC Larrys Creek Fish and Game Well Pad C. Rick Hall with EQT reported a spill had occurred on November 3, 2022 at 2000, that a water truck leaked about 10-20 gallons of production fluid while loading. Mr. Hall reported that a clean up crew was scheduled to remove the impacted soil. The area of excavation was about 30 ft. X 15 ft. and only about an inch of soil was scraped up to remove the impacted soil. The impacted soil was placed in a covered roll off dumpster onsite. The DEP screened the area of excavation with a soil conductivity meter and measured 10 uS/cm to 60 uS/cm. The DEP observed some rust and pitting on the production fluid tanks. A hole was also observed in the liner of the secondary containment for the production fluid tanks. The DEP recommends monitoring the production fluid tanks and repairing or replacing the tanks as necessary. The DEP also recommends repairing the hole in the liner of the secondary containment as soon as possible to avoid a inadvertent release. The spill of production fluid outside of containment to the well pad surface is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. These violations have been immediately corrected.

The report stated that no impacts to Waters of the Commonwealth occurred, and SPSI were on site conducting spill remediation.While on site, I spoke to a contractor with SPSI who stated that SPSI estimated the diesel fuel spill was approximately 50 gallons. SPSI utilized a PID meter to obtain VOC measurements of the impacted area. At the time of inspection, SPSI was actively excavating impacted aggregate and indicated that some areas within the delineated spill remained above 5 ppm. Further excavation would occur to achieve VOC readings below 5 ppm. SPSI planned to backfill the excavation once readings were below 5 ppm. While on site, I observed the following:-The Hunters Cave 3 OG Well Act 9 sign was located at the site entrance. A mailbox containing Emergency Response Plans (ERP), site plans, and a well permit was located at the site entrance (Photos 1-2).-The site entrance and access road appeared to be in generally good condition (Photo 3).-The diesel spill was located on the left side of the pad, outside of the perimeter of the sound barriers installed along the pad. The excavated area was approximately 20 ft x 20 ft, with a depth of 2-4 inches. SPSI was actively excavating impacted material at the time of inspection, and a PID meter was used to obtain VOC readings within the excavation (Photos 4-6).-A rolloff box was staged across from the spill, containing impacted aggregate that was excavated by SPSI. I observed inlet protection within both stormwater drains (Photos 9-10).-The well pad slopes on either side of the diesel fuel spill appeared to be in good condition, and I observed no indication that the diesel fuel spill exited the gravel pad (Photos 11-12).-A drilling rig was staged on site at the time of inspection (Photos 13-14).Due to the diesel fuel spill release exceeding 42 gallons (1 barrel), violations of 78.54, 91.34(A), and SWMA 301 are being issued to the Hunters Cave 3 OG Well.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/16/2021
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report from the operator of a brine leak at the tank battery of the #38448 well location (CID #355324). It appears as though ice accumulated within the diking and dislodged the drain line from the stock tank to the brine tank, allowing the tank to drain into the diking. Most of the fluid remained in containment, but a portion flowed out at a point of failure that had previously been noted in a 12/30/19 inspection of this site that had not been fixed. Elevated conductivity, in some places as high as >20 mS, was noted in puddles on the north and southwest corners of the site, and in the soil along the berm on the west side of the containment. The operator reported that 40 barrels of brine was released to containment. It is uncertain how much brine leaked outside of containment, but it is likely <1 barrel. The operator has disconnected the line from both tanks, closed the valves and put a bull plug in each. Per a phone call with Kirk Elkin of Diversified, they have already removed ~25 barrels of brine via vac truck, and will be mobilizing equipment to collect the rest of the brine and contaminated soil the week of 3/22/21. Further followup inspection will be done at that time.

CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Catalyst Energy Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-06-03
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 886007
Permit API: 083-55763
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-03
Comments: This well is a producing combination well with an electric powered motor attached. The well was being operated at the time of this inspection. The stuffing box gasket failed, and at the time of visit, the well was pumping oil and brine out to the ground. The fluid plus runoff from recent rains allowed the oil to flow down the road approximately 150 feet, entering a puddle near a culvert that carried an UNT Chappel Fork. The operator was contacted to get cleanup efforts underway. The well was shut off and pads were placed down to collect as much oil from the track as possible. No oil was apparent in the UNT. Rain stopped and there was a decrease in the flow of oil down the track. The pumper for this lease showed up and was able to leave and get a vacuum truck to come collect the water/oil in the puddle. Marking tape was placed so that public vehicles would not drive through the oil. It is estimated that 15-20 gallons of fluid, including 3-5 gallons of oil were released from the well due to the stuffing box failure. Most pooled in a low spot next to the wellhead. Some ran down the access road, again pooling in a puddle of water that was previously mentioned. The brine mostly stayed in place in the soil or vegetation. A puddle within 10 feet of the wellhead showed over 20 mS/cm conductivity, while checking further toward the extent of the spill showed much lower numbers. The final puddle registered under 0.1 mS/cm. The operator had the vac truck on the way and after later discussions, it was decided that they would need to excavate the area around the wellhead to remove impacted soil. Further follow up will be done on this site as possible.

Comments: On site today in response to a water complaint in the area. This is a FUI (Follow Up Inspection) for the (4) wells on the pad that were inspected on 10/14/21. They are the Howell 2H, 4H, 6H and 8H. All were in production at time of inspection. Remedial work was completed on the 2H, 4H and 6H wells at the end of 2017 to address previous violations cited on the 6H well. - Met w/ lease operator Ben Whitaker to perform isolated gas screenings of the cemented annuli. - All (4) wells have the (20x13) and (13x9) annuli isolated and venting to atmosphere. The (20x13) annuli are plumbed to surface via 3/8" SS tubing, the (13x9) and (9x5) annuli are plumbed to surface w/ 2" pipe. The (9x5) annuli are venting to a shared poly tank w/ an LEL of 100% and CH4 of 5%. Gas was detected in the(20x13) cemented annulus of the 6H and the 8H. Flow checks were performed by lease operator using an ALICAT micro flow meter. No gas flow was detected at any of these wells (20x13) or (13x9) cemented annuli. - The (20x13) and (13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad were left open and venting to atmosphere upon completion of gas screenings and flow checks. - Individual prod. casing pressures listed below: - 2H: 631 psi., capillary string - 4H: 618 psi., capillary string - 6H: 658 psi., capillary string - 8H: 660 psi. ** Although gas was detected at the (20x13) cemented annuli of the 6H and the 8H wells, no flow was detected via Cabots O&G's ALICAT micro flow meter. This appears to remain indicative of commingling, residual gas within the vent lines and/ or annular spaces. On 6/26/2021 Cabot O&G submitted a "Gas Migration Final Report" including a summary of previous remedial work performed on wells and an assessment of these residual gas detections. - No other violations or obvious concerns were noted.

Inspection Date: 6/03/2025
Comments: Inspection 2 of 2On 06/03/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the NV55HS Well Site following receipt of a spill report. The spill was reported to the Department on 06/02/2025 at 10:58am (CTS 389543). I was accompanied by Bruce Carpenter of CNX. Additional CNX representatives and SPSI were on site. The spill was reported to have occurred on 06/02/2025 at 7:30am. It was reported that produced water sprayed under the pad from one of the valves on the GPU. The release was contained and an unknown quantity was reported. No waterways were affected. The following was observed:Behind the GPU, a seep is present. Flow from this seep has allowed water to pool on the pad. This area was actively being vacuumed to remove any production fluid within the area. Absorbent materials were in use on site (Photos 1-3).Conductivity readings in the pooled area on the pad ranged from 375 uS/cm - 9.94 mS/cm (Photos 4-9).The water leads to a collection box on the pad, that outlets downslope of the pad. The shut off valve had been closed after the spill. No elevated conductivity was noted at the outlet off pad (Photos 10, 11).The operator updated the Department on 06/05/2025 that spill remediation has been completed. The Department requests an updated estimation of amount of fluid spilled. The Department also requests that a waste manifest be submitted as soon as possible. Due to the current estimated amount of fluid released being 4-5 gallons but threatening pollution to the Waters of the Commonwealth, and reporting the spill later than 2 hours after discovery, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) are being issued.

Wind is blowing from the southwest at an estimated 5 mph. Eight EWS Vox4 evaporators are in use at time of inspection. Comments: On October 2 2025, the Department conducted a complaint inspection in regards to CTS 392648. This gas well is currently under an Order (Enf ID 442909). This inspection is not evaluating the operator's compliance with the Order and is being conducted in response to the aforementioned complaint.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the access road and well site appeared to be stabilized with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well appeared equipped for production. A well tag was present on the well head and a well posting was present on a piece of the production equipment. There were no observed fluid leaks observed coming from the well head.Upon inspection of the production tank, the Department observed piping which ran to/from the production tank and the valve near the bottom of the tank, both of which appeared to be heavily corroded. It appeared a small about of fluid was seeping from the corroded portions of the piping onto the ground. The Department obtained a conductivity reading of the fluid on the pipe of 3.07mS. The Department obtained conductivity readings in the gravel below the corroded piping of 1.73ms and 0.87ms in an approximately 1 foot radius from the valve at the bottom of the production tank. These readings appear elevated in comparison to the Department's background conductivity reading of 0.22mS, indicating a release of production fluids has/is occurring.Prior to leaving the site, the Department attempted to contact the operator by calling the phone number on the well tag. The Department's call was sent to voicemail, and the Department was unable to leave a voicemail as the voicemail inbox was full.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed corroded production piping, as well as the observed release.

Permit API: 081-21879
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/19/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 9/18/23 a leak was discovered in a GPU on Pad A which led to the release of an unknown quantity of produced fluid to the pad surface. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad A. He showed me where the produced fluid leak occurred inside of GPU #3. He also showed me where the fluid overflowed the interior containment of the GPU and flowed outside of the GPU and onto the pad surface to the southwest of the GPU. A Waste Management crew was excavating the impacted area of the pad during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that the fluid appears to have traveled a couple of inches into the pad surface and then moved toward the southwest pad edge under the surface. A sump present in the stormwater channel along the southwest side of the pad had fluid in it with an electrical conductivity (EC) of 700 uS/cm. Mr. Subra stated that the initial EC reading taken in this sump was approximately 700 uS/cm and later it increased to approximately 1700 uS/cm. A smaller puddle of fluid approximately 25 feet to the north in the channel had an EC of 760 uS/cm during this inspection. No other fluid was observed in the channel or on the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming out the fluid in the southwest stormwater channel.Mr. Subra said that they plan to pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Environmental consultant Penn E and R was present during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that Penn E and R were performing electrical conductivity screening and would take samples for the Act 2 remediation. Violations noted against permit 081-21855 for the produced fluid release to the surface of Pad A.Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release to Pad B from 2/6/23.

Violation ID: 944928
Permit API: 015-23674
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Franklin Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2/11/2022
Comments: This Inspection Report cites violations for an apparent flowback (brine) release to the pad surface. The Analytical Report (attached) for SAC 942 metals shows 16.7 mg/L barium and 80.6 mg/L strontium in the liquid sample collected on February 1, 2022 (inspection 3315684). The narrative and findings in this report are from that previous inspection. I spoke with Justin Myers (Chief) on site. He explained that Cudd started drilling out plugs from the 5 Marcellus well heads today. They will have 3 coil tubing units on site to complete this job. Myers expects they will finish drilling the plugs in about 10 days. Workers are removing liner containment used while hydraulically fracturing the 5 Marcellus wells at this site. Pooled liquid on the south half of the pad surface has electrical conductivity of 14.1 - >19.99 mS/cm with an Oakton PCSTestr 35. I collected liquid sample 0935-430 in a 125 mL bottle and sent it to the DEP lab for SAC 942 metals analysis. The puddles across the south end of the pad are relatively shallow (<1/2" deep), so I did not fill a 500 mL bottle for inorganic element analysis. Violations could be cited pending laboratory sample analysis. Myers contacted Brendon Logan (Chief) to investigate the pooled liquid on the pad surface. I did not observe accelerated erosion or sedimentation during this inspection. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Air temp 26F JLP

Violation ID: 8271241
Permit API: 129-24171
Unconventional: No

Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/17/2026
Comments: On April 17, 2026, the DEP conducted a FUI of Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc's Armstrong 2 gas well following IR4155454 where violations were continued for an inadequately stabilized shared and direct access road. Present during today's inspection is DEP ET Rosie Wise.A NOV response has yet to be received from the operator of this gas well following IR3891447 when viols were issued however, the DEP has been in communication with the other operator who utilizes the shared portion of the access road. IR4155472 documents the other operator stating they would visit the site to assess the shared road. Observations collected of the shared access road during IR 4155454 include deep erosion rills with water actively flowing down the access road and an exposed and cracked open culvert pipe. During IR 4155454, the DEP requested the operator(s) provide the DEP with a written timeline of remedial actions to repair the access road. To date, this written timeline this has yet to be received. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the shared portion of the access road (Wildcat Road) to be graded with all erosion rills and the exposed culvert pipe removed. Dirt that appeared to be removed from the road during grading was observed to be piled up along the right side of the shared access road. Clumps of this dirt was also observed in the floodway/streambank of a stream located directly downslope and to the right of the shared access road. The broken culvert pipe was observed to be lying on the ground adjacent to the access road, another piece of culvert piping that the broken piece was connected to was still observed to be in the ground and partially buried. Water was not observed to be actively discharging out of this culvert outlet as it appears the inlet may be blocked and resulting in seepage of water along other portions of the access road downslope. The DEP notes that no E and S controls appeared to be installed anywhere along the shared access road. Violations are being issued at this time for sediment entering the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) and for failure to install E and S controls during earth disturbance activity.At the time of this inspection, no other active E and S issues were observed along the shared portions of Wildcat Road, however, the shared road was not stabilized with gravel and is exhibiting the potential for other E and S issues to occur.The DEP recommends the Operator remove the sediment from the WOC, stabilize the access road, unblock/replace the culvert pipe and install E and S controls along the access road to prevent any further e and s issues.Upon inspection of the direct portion of the access road, conditions appear to be unchanged, the DEP observed large areas of the access road to be flooded. An exposed pipe was observed alongside the access road, however no methane or other odor was detected, the exposed portion of the pipe did not appear to be compromised.At the time of this inspection, the gas well site was still observed to be overgrown with vegetation. A well tag with all required information posted on it was observed to be fixed to a heavily rusted wellhead. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the gas wellhead or other production equipment on site at this time, however, a strong gas odor and hissing sound was observed to be coming from the lower portion of the gas wellhead. OGI assistance is being requested at this time to assess the gas wellhead for a gas release. Refer to IR 4183514 for the continuation of violations for heavily rusted production equipment.While onsite, the DEP called the number on the well tag in an attempt to notify the operator of the new violations, however, the number was not in service. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for an inadequately stabilized access road are being continued, and new violations are being issued for sediment entering WOC and failure to implement E and S controls.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2022
Comments: This unconventional well is currently housed within a cellar (onto which a well tag has been affixed) and appears to be shut in. There is no infrastructure or equipment on the well site that would indicate that the well is (or has ever been) able to be produced. This well was spud on 8/18/2011, all submitted production reports for this well since that time indicate that the well has not been produced. The Department does not appear to have received a well log/record or completion report for this well. There is a second well (047-24582) on this pad, which was plugged in August of 2013. Pin Oak has failed to restore this well site according to approved plans associated with ESX11-047-0022 and more than nine months have passed since the completion of drilling of this well and the plugging of 047-24582. The site ID sign for this well site is located at the end of the spur road that leads to this well. This sign does not meet the requirements of 78a.55(4). The access road leading to this well site is in suitable condition for the limited traffic that is currently using it. Maintenance/improvements to the road surface should be considered prior to any heavy equipment use of the road given its proximity to the West Branch of the Clarion River. Vegetative cover around the perimeter of the well site and the access road banks appears to be established, future inspections will be conducted during the upcoming growing season to further evaluate the stabilization of earth disturbance associated with this well site.

Violation ID: 8287342
Permit API: 015-23881
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/27/2026
Comments: The weather was 73 degrees and sunny at the time of this inspection. The above-referenced gas well is currently listed as Active in eFACTS. The purpose of this inspection is to evaluate well integrity at the end of a 72-hour pressure build-up test. Six(6) Unconventional gas wells have been spud on the Pad. The Well Record and required mechanical integrity assessments have been submitted to the Department. No excessive corrosion observed during the inspection. There was a pressure gauge observed at this well during the inspection that read 812psi on the production casing. ¿¿ Jason Rajan of Creston Environmental accompanied me during the inspections to record pressures, monitor for combustible gas, and collect gas samples from the annuli where sufficient gas was present for isotopic analysis. At the conclusion of testing at the above-referenced well, pressures were measured with a crystal pressure gauge and recorded prior to opening each annulus vent. Each annulus vent was immediately checked for presence/absence of combustible gas using Creston's Bascom Turner GasExplorer meter (calibrated 8/27/2026). The monitoring results were as follows: ¿¿ * Conductor by Surface casing (20" X 13 3/8") – final pressure = 0.0psi¿¿ with 2% LEL and 0% Methane ¿¿ * Surface by Intermediate casing (13 3/8" X 9 5/8") – final pressure = 2.64psi with 100% LEL and 24% Methane. ¿¿ * Intermediate by Production casing (9 5/8" X 5 1/2") – final pressure = 236.1psi with 100% LEL and 85% Methane. ¿¿ Gas samples were collected by Creston for isotopic analysis from the 9 5/8" x 5 1/2" and 13 3/8" x 9 5/8" annulus vents. A gas sample was not collected from the 20" x 13 3/8" annulus vent. ¿¿ The area immediately surrounding the well head was also monitored for combustible gas using an Altair 5X combustible gas meter (calibrated 7/28/2026). The results of this monitoring indicated that 0% LEL and 0% Methane was measured during the inspection. Violations are continued from original date of 5/01/2025. No new violations were noted at this inspection.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/08/2022 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Wyalusing Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/24/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 951237
Permit API: 015-23689
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wyalusing Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/08/2022
Comments: On 4/8/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine/complete inspection at the Chesapeake Solowiej well site. It was 45¿ and sunny when I started the inspection. Rainfall had occurred across the region during the last 24 hours and water puddles were present on the pad surface. I field tested some of these for conductance with an Oakton PCTS 50 with the results of 0.643 mS or less. There were areas of disturbance that lacked adequate stabilization noted along each wall of the perimeter berm. A sediment trap is installed on site. At the beginning of the inspection I had a conversation with the landowner, Mr. Solowiej about the sediment trap and where the outfall was located. The outlet pipe travels underground approximately 190 feet outside the permitted limits of disturbance to the stream that follows Riverview Road south of the well site. We also discussed the path of the stream as it travels across his farm and continues to the Susquehanna River. The stream bypasses the pond on his farmstead. The construction of the sediment trap and discharge outfall is not consistent with the ESCGP and is in violation of Section 401 of the Clean Streams Law for discharging directly to the Waters of the Commonwealth and of 102.5(m)4 for failure to comply with the terms and conditions of the E & S Control General Permit. There were three wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The Solowiej 1HC well is full of water that field tested at 1.172 conductance. The production tank had secondary containment. There is a pile of residual waste from site excavation on site in secondary containment. The DEP recommends the following: 1. Remove the water from the 1HC well cellar. 2. Provide updated plans for the sediment trap, underflow piping and outlet to the department. 3. Assess the existing dimensions of the sediment trap to ensure that it is adequately sized for the area it services. 4. Properly dispose of the pile of residual waste when conditions allow. 5. Followup with permitting to determine if there are Chapter 105 unpermitted impacts. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3326981 I left the site at 11:00.

Comments: On 5/30/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Grippo well site. It was 73 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Temporary stabilization has been applied to some areas of the perimeter berm. PCSM is addressed by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed. Temporary compost filter socks remain in place down slope from the infiltration areas.There were five wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The production tank had secondary containment.No violations were noted during the inspection. I did not witness any visible evidence of spills or leaks during the inspection.Violations are still outstanding for the following: inspection ID 3543791 for the release of fluid with elevated conductance to the pad surface during production operations; inspection ID 3529982 for elevated conductance fluid being discovered on the unprotected pad surface; and inspection ID 3517519 for high conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface after fracking operations and for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface during drilling operations.I left the site at 1430 hours.

Comments: Onsite for a routine inspection. A 100bbl steel tank within the earthen dike (not hooked up) has developed a large rusty blister and was observed to be leaking fluid down the side of the tank. Bryan Deitz from Diversified Gas and Oil was contacted. Bryan indicated that a water truck will be sent out to empty the tank. A 50bbl poly tank is plumbed to the separator. The violation has been corrected.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's DCNR 587 02-003 well site located in Ward Township, Tioga County on 2/1/2023 at 1540 hours. The weather was 26 degrees with clear skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a reported release called in by Repsol.On 2/1/2023 at ~1335 hours, a release of ~5 barrels of produced water, ice and sand was discovered by Repsol after a line on a sand trap froze and split. Water, ice and sand was release to the pad surface near the wellheads onsite (photos #1 and 2). Sand, ice and dirt was recovered and placed in a 55-gallon drum for later disposal. The release mixed with onsite stormwater that was held in and around the well cellars. An onsite vacuum truck recovered a reported 1000 gallons of stormwater mixed with the produced water from the cellars and impacted area. I field measured all of the fluids in and around the impacted area for electrical conductivity utilizing an Oakton PCTS 50 meter. All readings ranged from 400 to 680us/cm today. Based on the reported release of ~5 barrels of produced water to the pad surface, new violations of the following are cited against API #117-22101 at this time:35 P.S. 691.402(b)25 Pa. Code78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.301Violations cited against API #117-22101 on 7/27/2022 remain outstanding at this time. I departed the site at 1615 hours.

Code §78a.73(b), §78a81(a)(2) and (3), and §78a.85(a)(5) have been cited. Please note that because your company provided a self-reported notification, no violation was cited for 25 Pa.
